title: Duals of complexes with finite locally constant cohomology
statement:
Let $\lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, let $T$ be a scheme on which
$\ell$ is invertible, and let $C$ be an ordinary
bounded derived complex
of etale $\lambda$-sheaves. Suppose all $\mathcal H^q(C)$
are finite locally constant. Its
derived internal dual
$C^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_\lambda(C,\lambda_T)$ has finite locally
constant cohomology, with

$$
\mathcal H^q(C^\vee)
=\mathcal Hom_\lambda(\mathcal H^{-q}(C),\lambda_T).
$$

For every scheme morphism $v:T'\to T$, the canonical morphism
$v^*C^\vee\to (v^*C)^\vee$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Convert the existing global cohomology bounds [a,b] to DerivedCategory.IsGE a and IsLE b using isGE_iff and isLE_iff. The coefficient ring ULift (ZMod ell) is a finite field. Apply the already fully proved adopted theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.isFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf_homology_coefficientDual in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.Derived.LisseFieldDual, with the unchanged finite-lisse cohomology hypothesis, to obtain both finite local constancy of the dual cohomology and its degree-reversed internal-Hom formula. This adopted proof is the truncation devissage through dualizable finite-lisse cohomology sheaves, not a use of the auxiliary site-perfect calculation.

Apply the already proved isIso_coefficientDualComparison_of_isFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf from the same adopted module, with those same bounds and cohomology hypothesis. Its coefficientDualComparison is definitionally the existing finiteLisseDualPullbackComparison: both are derivedHomUpperStarComparison followed by the internal-Hom functor applied to leftDerivedUpperStarUnitIso. Thus the exact canonical comparison in the node is invertible, without changing any definition or statement. No hypothesis about invertibility of ell is needed by this stronger adopted result; the existing hypothesis is retained verbatim.
